answers_review: ts23_review5.json (FAIL: LONE_CR_IGNORED_BY_SUITE, UNTERMINATED_LINE_COUNTED_AS_NEWLINE, EMPTY_QUEUE_REPORTS_BUDGET, UTF8_HEADINGS_DROPPED, G2_CWD_STILL_MISMATCHED, FALSE_CATCH_ONE_STEP_CRASH, CACHE_DELETION_UNVERIFIED, ATX_CLOSING_SEQUENCE_UNSPECIFIED)
admission: The four survivors were not implementation bugs so much as UNSPECIFIED BEHAVIOUR: the requirement never said what a lone CR counts as, whether an unterminated last line is a newline, whether non-ASCII headings count, or what an empty queue reports. An unspecified behaviour cannot fail a test, which is why a wrong answer passed. So this round pins the semantics instead of patching around them. That is TT-R14-040.

semantics_now_pinned.newlines: a line terminator is LF, CRLF or a lone CR; the count is terminators, not lines, so a trailing terminator counts and an unterminated final line does not
semantics_now_pinned.atx: levels 1..6 count, 7 or more hashes is not a heading, and an ATX closing sequence (space + hashes) is stripped from the text
semantics_now_pinned.utf8: non-ASCII heading text is kept as is
semantics_now_pinned.empty_queue: steps 0, remaining 0, reviews [], halt_reason QUEUE_EXHAUSTED - nothing was queued, so nothing was budget-limited

changes.fix: the implementation counts terminators (LF + CR - CRLF) and the test pins a lone-CR file (3) and an unterminated file (1), each asserting the precondition that the file really contains the bytes it claims
changes.evidence: both mutations now fail with AssertionErrors

changes.fix: the fixture contains a CJK heading and an '## Beta ##' line; the implementation strips the closing sequence and the test's expectation applies the same rule
changes.evidence: both mutations fail; the CJK heading and 'Beta' (not 'Beta ##') are asserted

changes.fix: an empty queue is now a case: steps 0, remaining 0, reviews [], halt_reason QUEUE_EXHAUSTED
the test runs in the same cwd as the probe, and a crash is detected by any exception class in the assertion message, not only by a traceback header
changes.evidence: self-test with a ZeroDivisionError mutant that carries no traceback header: caught=false, crash_not_evidence=true, false_red=true, harness exit 1

changes.fix: the purge no longer ignores errors and asserts that no __pycache__ remains; a failed purge raises instead of leaving stale bytecode
changes.evidence: harness runs clean with the assertion active
